messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: high error rate observed from inference-gateway in us-west-2. 5xx spike starting ~00:04 UTC, elevated latencies, customer-facing timeouts. Root thread created for live mitigation and hypothesis tracking.

eng-oncall: I'm on it. looking at the dashboard now. can someone confirm if this is host-level or model-level?

sara: I'm taking lead. assigning miguel to logs and jake to infra. @carol can you ping CS for customers in the impacted region?

miguel: pulling logs for gateway and runtime. initial grep: `grep -E "ERROR|timeout|kvcache" /var/log/redwood/gateway/*.log | tail -n 200`

miguel: snippet from gateway: ```
2026-03-15T00:03:58Z ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream_timeout route=/v1/completions client=acme-corp
2026-03-15T00:04:02Z WARN kv-cache miss key=usr-ctx-42
2026-03-15T00:04:05Z ERROR request_id=abc124 downstream=runtime code=502 msg=upstream read error
```

jake: infra metrics show a sustained increase in queue length on pod inference-runtime-7 for model-redwood-7b-q4. CPU stable, GPU memory near 88% on that node. No node restarts.

sara: timeline so far: 00:02 UTC small bump in tail-latency; 00:03 full spike in 5xx; 00:07 partial recovery on some routes.

carol: CS notified initial customers in us-west-2, two reported degraded completions. collecting request ids.

eng-oncall: hypothesis tracking — let's capture everything in-thread. H1: model runtime kernel regression (new kernel rollout). H2: KV cache eviction cascade causing downstream timeouts. H3: network egress throttling to storage. H4: client-side sudden traffic spike (unrelated).

miguel: logs from package deployer show a canary rollout finished at 23:55 UTC of a runtime patch `infer-runtime v1.12.3` -> 1.12.4 on subset of pods. that fits H1.

jake: checking rollout state: ```kubectl -n inference get deploy infer-runtime -o yaml | grep image: -n``` shows mix of 1.12.3 and 1.12.4 across replicas.

miguel: correlation: pods with 1.12.4 have higher `handler_error` counts in logs. patch looks suspicious.

sara: quick mitigation plan: 1) scale up 1.12.3 pods and mark 1.12.4 as pause; 2) fallback routing to cheaper model-variant for affected customers; 3) collect full kv-cache metrics and dump. who owns rollback? jake?

jake: I can do a scoped revert for the canary. will cordon the 1.12.4 pods and restart them into 1.12.3 image to test revert. prepping command: `kubectl set image deploy/infer-runtime infer-runtime=redwood/infer-runtime:1.12.3 --record`

ops-bot: runbook note: rollback must be limited to us-west-2 canary node pool to avoid global disruption. follow with `checklist: healthcheck, smoke tests, watch 1xx/2xx rates`

sara: also test KV: miguel please dump KV cache hit-rate and eviction logs with `redis-cli --stat` and `REDWOOD_KV_DUMP=1` on suspect nodes.

miguel: dumping now, partial output: ```
# redis INFO keyspace
db0:keys=120345,expires=0,avg_ttl=0
# eviction metrics
evicted_keys: 0
# but observed high miss rate per prefix: user-ctx-* miss_rate=0.67
```

sara: that makes H2 less likely to be eviction-driven but high miss_rate could still exacerbate load. keep as secondary.

carol: customer update: acme-corp provided request ids abc123, abc124. they saw timeouts, asked for ETA. CS requests targeted mitigation asap and follow-up postmortem.

sara: OK run revert test to validate H1. jake please execute rollback on canary, miguel and I will watch errors and latencies. set a 5-min observation window.

jake: executing: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/infer-runtime --to-revision=2026031501 -n inference --record` on canary nodes.

jake: done. pods cycling... 00:11 UTC pods back to 1.12.3 (canary pool).

miguel: observing logs post-rollback: ```
2026-03-15T00:11:25Z INFO request_id=abc200 upstream=runtime code=200 latency=120ms
2026-03-15T00:11:30Z INFO kv-cache hit key=usr-ctx-42
```

eng-oncall: immediate metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 3.8% -> 0.5% in canary pool within 90s. Latency p50 improved ~120ms.

sara: verdict: H1 validated for canary. next: plan for wider remediation. options: a) full rollback in us-west-2, b) pause rollout and health-check with earlier image and run regression tests, c) apply hotfix to 1.12.4 if root cause identified quickly.

jake: recommending staged rollback across us-west-2 with traffic steering to other regions where safe. I'll own rollout orchestration. ETA 20-30m for region-wide rollback.

miguel: meanwhile collecting last 24h of traces for postmortem and saving to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1929001234/trace_dump.tar.gz. command: `tar czf /tmp/trace_dump.tar.gz /var/log/redwood/* && aws s3 cp /tmp/trace_dump.tar.gz s3://...`

carol: CS update queued: "We identified a problematic runtime canary and have reverted it in the affected region. We expect service to stabilize; will follow up with detailed RCA." :thumbsup:

sara: owners and action items (in-thread):
- H1 owner: jake (rollback orchestration, region rollout)
- H1 validation: miguel + sara (logs & metrics)
- H2 follow-up: miguel (KV metrics trace, regen caching telemetry)
- RCA doc: sara to draft, attach traces + timeline
- Postmortem due: 72h, assign to incident owner pool

eng-oncall: logging experiment plan (to validate root cause): create canary of 1.12.4 with debug logging enabled on one isolated node and run a synthetic traf load for 20 min. owner: miguel. revert if errors spike.

sara: final note: maintain communication to CS and affected customers. once rollback completes, monitor 30m and then close incident channel. Great cross-team response. :pray:

incident-bot: Incident closed for channel reminders: add `incident-1929001234` tag to internal docs and schedule postmortem meeting.
